scale: 1 = weak, 3 = solid, 5 = offer-ready at a top consulting firm

dimensions.name: Structure
dimensions.1: No framework, or a memorized one that does not fit the case.
dimensions.3: A sensible framework that covers most of the problem, somewhat generic.
dimensions.5: A tailored, MECE framework built for this case, prioritized, and used to drive the rest of the case.

dimensions.name: Clarifying questions
dimensions.1: Jumps in without confirming the objective or scope.
dimensions.3: Asks a few useful questions; confirms the objective.
dimensions.5: Asks sharp, targeted questions (objective, scope, timeline, business model) and uses the answers.

dimensions.name: Quantitative / math
dimensions.1: Skips the math or gets key numbers wrong.
dimensions.3: Gets most numbers right, sometimes slowly or with prompting.
dimensions.5: Sets up calculations clearly out loud, gets them right, and says what each number means.

dimensions.name: Business judgment
dimensions.1: Ignores the data or draws conclusions that do not follow.
dimensions.3: Reasonable conclusions; misses some risks or second-order effects.
dimensions.5: Uses data to find the real driver, weighs trade-offs and risks, thinks like an owner.

dimensions.name: Synthesis / recommendation
dimensions.1: No clear recommendation, or just repeats facts.
dimensions.3: Gives a recommendation with some support.
dimensions.5: Leads with a clear answer, backs it with 2-3 numbers, names risks and next steps.

dimensions.name: Communication
dimensions.1: Hard to follow; rambles or goes silent.
dimensions.3: Clear most of the time; occasionally disorganized.
dimensions.5: Concise, signposted ('I'd look at three things...'), and checks in with the interviewer.
